title: Cost-efficient tier: aggressive batching + burst guardrails to prevent queue blowups
author: Marcus Reed
release_notes: Runtime: cost-efficient batching tier is more throughput-oriented (larger target batches) with new safeguards under burst/overload (bounded queue growth, backpressure escalation, and automatic batch-size clamp).
description: Summary: This PR tunes the cost-efficient SLO tier to prefer larger, more GPU-efficient batches (especially on decode-heavy traffic), while adding guardrails that prevent unbounded queue growth during bursts. Motivation: Early perf runs for the tiered defaults showed meaningful $/1K token improvements from more aggressive batching, but the naive configuration can create queue blowups under sudden concurrency spikes (tail latency + timeouts + cascading retries). For the cost-efficient tier we explicitly accept higher latency, but we still need bounded behavior and predictable degradation (backpressure/load shedding) so that bursty customers don’t take the whole cluster into a retry storm. Changes: (1) More aggressive batching targets for cost-efficient tier: increase target_batch_tokens for decode, allow larger max_batch_tokens for compatible model families, bias scheduler toward forming fuller decode batches when queue is healthy. (2) Burst guardrails: add queue depth / queued tokens hard caps for the cost-efficient tier; when exceeded, we escalate through overload modes (clamp batch growth -> tighten max_wait_ms -> admission control) rather than continuing to accumulate queued work. (3) Backpressure behavior: introduce a cost-efficient-only "soft reject" path that returns 429 with Retry-After when the queue caps are exceeded, instead of accepting requests that are likely to timeout. (4) Stability knobs: add a per-tier "burst_window_ms" accounting mechanism so short spikes don’t immediately trip hard load shedding; instead we allow a small debt window before escalating. (5) Metrics: add counters/gauges to observe queue caps and overload escalations (tier labeled, with cardinality-safe tags). Non-goals: this PR does not add profile selection reason codes (tracked in ENG-18426 / PR-28473), and it does not change fast-tier tail protection (ENG-18424 / PR-28458). Default values (cost-efficient only, subject to further tuning in benchmark-lab): - max_batch_tokens: 8192 -> 16384 (model-family dependent; guarded by existing model metadata for max supported batch tokens) - target_decode_batch_tokens: 4096 -> 8192 - max_wait_ms: 8ms (unchanged) but dynamically clamped to 4ms in overload mode 1 - queue_max_queued_tokens: new, default 2 * max_batch_tokens - queue_max_queued_requests: new, default 512 (primarily for tiny prompts) - burst_window_ms: new, default 250ms Bench results (local A100 + H100 sanity + mixed workload replay; see linked perf artifacts): - Throughput: +12–18% tokens/sec vs previous cost-efficient candidate profile on decode-heavy mixes - Median latency: +3–7% (expected trade-off) - Tail behavior under burst: p99 stabilized vs prior candidate (previously saw multi-second tail due to queue growth; now bounded with 429s under sustained overload) Testing: - Added unit tests for overload state machine transitions and queue cap enforcement. - Added integration test that simulates burst concurrency ramp and asserts queue caps prevent unbounded queue growth. - Ran perf suite scenario "mixed_workload_cost_efficient" with 3 seeds; results attached in CI artifacts. Rollout: guarded behind existing tiered defaults feature flag; no behavior change unless cost-efficient tier is enabled. Notes for SRE: cost-efficient tier will surface 429s earlier under sustained overload rather than timing out; this is intentional and aligns with predictable degradation guidance in the rollout playbook. Follow-ups: - PR-28492 will further constrain metric cardinality for tier labels once the final taxonomy is locked. - Consider raising queue_max_queued_requests for embedding-like workloads once we have separate tier profiles per route type (not in scope).
commits: scheduler: increase cost-efficient tier batching targets for decode-heavy traffic
scheduler: add queue caps + overload escalation state machine for cost-efficient tier
runtime: implement 429 Retry-After backpressure path on queue cap exceed
metrics: export queue cap hits + overload transitions (tier-labeled)
tests: add unit + integration coverage for burst guardrails
bench: add mixed workload scenario config for cost-efficient tier validation
review_conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): The direction looks right, but I’m worried about queue_max_queued_tokens being expressed as 2x max_batch_tokens globally. For small models we’ll hit the cap too early and shed load more aggressively than necessary. Can we make the cap proportional to in-flight decode concurrency instead? Marcus Reed (author): Good call. I added burst_window_ms and made the cap scale with "effective_decode_parallelism" (defaults to scheduler’s current estimate, bounded). I kept the 2x as a fallback if the estimate is unavailable. Added tests for both code paths. Omar El-Sayed (review): The clamp from 8ms -> 4ms in overload mode 1 makes sense. Please confirm we don’t starve long-prefill requests when cost-efficient is mixed with other tiers on the same worker. Marcus Reed (author): Confirmed: the clamp is tier-scoped and only affects queues tagged cost-efficient. The global anti-starvation logic remains unchanged. I also added a regression test with mixed short/long prefill showing forward progress for long requests. Sean Gallagher (review): From an SRE perspective, returning 429 is preferable to timeouts, but we need metric signals to page/triage (cap hits rate, overload mode duration). Are these exported and tagged safely? Marcus Reed (author): Added scheduler_queue_cap_hits_total, scheduler_overload_mode (gauge), and scheduler_overload_transitions_total. Tags: tier + region; model is not included to avoid cardinality blowups. Allison Grant (review): Please ensure the metric names match the taxonomy draft and that tier labeling is consistent with the other PRs. Also, can we add a log line on first transition into overload mode? Marcus Reed (author): Updated names to match the draft taxonomy. Added rate-limited structured log on first transition per worker per minute (includes tier, overload_mode, queue_depth, queued_tokens). Lena Fischer (review): Can we keep the default values conservative until benchmark-lab runs land? I’d prefer max_batch_tokens 16384 only where we have validated kernels and memory headroom. Marcus Reed (author): Agreed. I gated 16384 behind model metadata (max_batch_tokens_supported) and defaulted to 8192 for unknown families; updated config comments and added a validation check in schema loading. Sofia Ivanova (final): LGTM after the scaling change + tests. Sean Gallagher (final): Approved; please link this in the rollout checklist so oncall knows to expect earlier 429s for cost-efficient. Marcus Reed (author): Done (added note in internal overload_modes doc; rollout checklist link will be updated in the Drive doc separately).
